newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanshin Construction misses payment.
newsitem.headline: Hanshin Construction misses payment.

text.p: A major South Korean construction company which filed for court receivership on Friday has missed debt payments on 21.8 billion won in promissory notes, an official from its main creditor bank told Reuters on Saturday.
A SEOULBANK official said Hanshin Construction Co, the country's 24th largest construction firm, had 21.8 billion won in notes that came due on Saturday.
Unless Hanshin pays the notes by the close of business on Monday, the bank official said the company would be in what is known as first default.
In Korea, a company is declared insolvent on the third default.
SEOULBANK earlier said the bank would provide no additional credits to Hanshin because it believed the company's financial condition would worsen, the bank official said.
Hanshin, the country's 50th largest company overall, sought court protection on Friday after determining it would not be able to pay its debts, said company spokesman Ha Dong-woo.

He said Hanshin, which has three affiliates, had assets of 1.28 trillion won versus liabilities of 1.99 trillion won and capital stock of 84.7 billion. Hanshin's debt to equity ratio was 598 percent, said Ha.
The Korea Stock exchange said trading of Hanshin Construction stocks had been suspended for Saturday's half-session and would resume under supervision from Monday. ($1 = 890 won)
